newsitem.title: USA: Clinton - U.S. may take part in new Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: Clinton - U.S. may take part in new Bosnia force.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday it was conceivable that the United States could take part in a follow-up international force in Bosnia but he was awaiting detailed NATO recommendations on that force.

"It is conceivable that we could participate but it depends upon exactly what the recommendation is," Clinton told a news conference. The mandate of the current NATO-led IFOR mission runs out on December 20 and NATO is working on detailed options for a possible follow-up mission.
Clinton said: "We would like to see ... what our contribution would be. I'm going to assess the risks as I always do and the possible benefits. and then I will make a judgment."

He added: "Whether we can do this ... will depend on what the nature of the mission is. I'm looking forward to the NATO report. I haven't received it yet." Clinton had earlier pledged to pull the U.S. troops out of Bosnia by the end of this year, but NATO military officials are in the final stages of drawing up contingency plans on a possible post-IFOR force.

The United States is now sending into Bosnia a force of more than 5,000 troops, some of whom will stay until mid-March, to cover the withdrawl of 15,000 Americans now there as part of the international IFOR force of 50,000.

NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, on a visit to the Bosnian capital Sarajevo, made clear to reporters NATO would remain involved in the country as it struggles to rebuild after years of war. "NATO will not abandon Bosnia," he told a news conference.
